name: The Mindless Ones

meta.next: Rattling the Rattlecages, The Damned (Classic), Class quests

summary: Newly risen Forsaken face the Mindless Ones on Deathknell's northern edge. Shadow Priest Sarvis sends them to cull Mindless Zombies and Wretched Zombies, Scourge thralls bound to the Lich King's command.

sections.title: Slaves to the Frozen Throne
sections.body: Many who rise from Lordaeron's dirt never recover their minds. The Forsaken broke free of Ner'zhul's domination as his power waned, but countless corpses remain chained to his will. In northern Deathknell, Mindless Zombies and Wretched Zombies wander, driven to violence. For you, newly risen among the undead, putting them down is the first hard trial. You prove your freedom by ending the thrall of those who never escaped.

sections.title: Mercy Through Destruction
sections.body: Shadow Priest Sarvis grieves that these legions of dead cannot strengthen the Forsaken's desperate struggle. There is no cure for them. Their minds are broken, and they remain instruments of slaughter. If left to roam, they bring chaos to Deathknell's doorstep and give the Lich King easy fodder. Destroying them is necessary for the settlement and brings a grim end to some of Lordaeron's fallen.

faq.q: Why can't the mindless zombies be recruited into the Forsaken?
faq.answer: The zombies cannot choose to join Lady Sylvanas because their minds are broken and bound to the Lich King. Shadow Priest Sarvis says their numbers would be invaluable, but they remain dangerous Scourge thralls.

The zombies were human inhabitants of Lordaeron who fell to the plague of undeath during the Third War. Unlike you, they never regained their memories, personalities, or freedom of choice when the Lich King's grip slipped.

faq.q: Why is Shadow Priest Sarvis commanding the defense here?
faq.answer: Shadow Priest Sarvis oversees the first days of newly risen undead in Deathknell. He judges whether they have the grit and clear mind to survive their new existence.

faq.q: What is the difference between Forsaken and Scourge zombies?
faq.answer: Forsaken have free will, while Scourge zombies do not. Forsaken escaped the Lich King's telepathic control and kept their intelligence and emotions; he directly puppeteers the empty vessels of the Scourge.

faq.q: Are the mindless zombies a threat to Deathknell?
faq.answer: Yes. These zombies wander just north of Deathknell, threatening new arrivals from the graves and the Forsaken priests trying to organize the settlement.

faq.q: Where does this task lead next?
faq.answer: Your success against the mindless dead leads to more duties securing Deathknell, including culling skeletal Scourge in Rattling the Rattlecages and beginning training with your class mentor.

angles.text: As an Undead, you may see a former neighbor, kin, or friend among the zombies roaming the village outskirts. They remind you what you were spared and what could happen if the Forsaken fall.
As a Priest, you serve under Shadow Priest Sarvis and meet the Forsaken's pragmatic, shadow-tinged way of life, adopted in place of the Holy Light that abandoned them.
As a member of the Horde, you see why the Horde once viewed the Forsaken with deep suspicion before admitting them to the faction.
